clue.text: Innkeeper makes one lie in other building

indicators.note: in tells us the word lie sits inside the rearranged letters
building is read as constructing something new, so the letters of 'other' are put together in a fresh order

parts.note: the word other supplies the letters to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A landlord persuades someone to tell an untruth inside a different property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun for the property, but it is the anagram signal; 'makes one' merely links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps an inn runs a hotel, so they are the hotel's proprietor.

clue.text: Founder's church is in right surroundings

definitions.note: the clue's 's is read as 'is', so the definition is the founder of a faith, followed by a link word

indicators.note: in says the word is goes inside the abbreviation for right
surroundings says the abbreviation for right wraps round the word is

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sentence about a founder's church standing amid the right setting.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the 's of 'Founder's' as 'is', a link word; 'in' and 'surroundings' together signal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus is regarded as the founder of the faith that bears his title.

clue.text: Carol's little town

parts.note: the carol 'O Little Town of ...' names this town in its very first line

explanation.surface: It reads like a woman named Carol and her small home town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, but it is a song sung at the festive season: the carol 'O Little Town of Bethlehem'.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's first line addresses the small town in Judea where the nativity took place.

clue.text: Reign shown by star moving above cupola, leaving East

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places the first piece over the second
moving says the letters of star shift into a new order

parts.note: the word star supplies the letters

indicators.note: leaving says one letter departs from the word for a cupola

parts.note: a cupola is a dome

explanation.surface: A reign is shown by a star travelling over a domed roof and heading away from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges STAR into TSAR; 'leaving' takes E (East) out of DOME, leaving DOM; 'above' puts TSAR over DOM in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The period or realm of rule of an emperor of Russia is called by this name, so it means a reign.

clue.text: Pan panto character Simon

definitions.meaning: the boy who never grew up is ... Pan, a staple of British Christmas pantomime
the apostle Simon was renamed by Jesus

explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime is a comic family stage show put on in Britain around the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the pantomime hero Pan and the apostle Simon share this first name.

clue.text: Cold that hangs about now?

definitions.meaning: a heavy cold with a runny nose is said to be a streaming one
a festive decoration of paper ribbon hangs across rooms at this season

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like an adjective about weather; it is a head cold that makes the nose run.
explanation.definitionFit: A long paper ribbon is hung up as decoration, and a running cold can be called by the same word.

clue.text: Commercial opening that covers four Sundays

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an AD
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: An advert that launches something over a month of weekends.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season before the Nativity spans the four Sundays leading up to the feast.

clue.text: Character who made 'The More It Snows' ring round

definitions.text: Character who made 'The More It Snows'

indicators.note: round says the word for a ring is turned the other way about

parts.note: a hoop is a ring

explanation.surface: A character who composed a snowy song makes it ring out all around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' reverses HOOP. A. A. Milne's bear hums 'The more it snows, tiddely pom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Milne's honey-loving bear composes the hum 'The More It Snows' in The House at Pooh Corner.

clue.text: Diner consumes seconds — change diet for period after religious festival

indicators.note: consumes says the diner swallows up the abbreviation for seconds

parts.note: a diner is an eater

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of diet

parts.note: the word diet supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Someone eating takes second helpings, then has to rethink their diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' signals the container and 'change' the anagram; 'for' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The season following the spring feast of the Resurrection is named for it with the old word for time.

clue.text: Understand pressure on the woman after start of festive month

indicators.note: after says the rest follows the first piece

parts.note: the first day of December is Dec 1, written DEC plus the numeral I
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
the woman is her

explanation.surface: Grasping the strain placed on a woman once the festive month begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of festive month' is 1 December, written DEC I with the Roman numeral, not just the first letter of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode something is to make sense of it, which is to understand it.

clue.text: Team members needed to carry out piping

definitions.meaning: a cricket or football side has this many players, so the number names the team

definitions.text: members needed to carry out piping
definitions.meaning: in the carol 'The Twelve Days of Christmas' there are this many pipers piping

explanation.walkthrough: In the carol, the true love sends this many pipers piping on the eleventh day.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side is named after its number of players, the same number of pipers in the carol.

clue.text: Plant removed from motel site

indicators.note: removed is read as re-moved, moved again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: these two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A shrub that has been dug up and taken away from a motel's grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' reads as re-moved: the letters of MOTEL SITE are moved round.
explanation.definitionFit: This parasitic evergreen with white berries is a plant, hung up for kissing under at the festive season.

clue.text: Like the sherry decanter by the time gran's jolly vacant?

definitions.text: Like the sherry decanter by the time gran's jolly
definitions.meaning: once grandmother is merry, the sherry has all been drunk

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a joke: by the time gran is tipsy, the decanter has been drained.
explanation.definitionFit: A drained decanter holds nothing, and something vacant is likewise unoccupied and has nothing in it.

clue.text: He takes a bow in pantomime

definitions.text: He takes a bow in pantomime

parts.words: He takes a bow in pantomime
parts.note: the outlaw of Sherwood Forest is an archer carrying a bow, and a favourite subject for festive pantomime

explanation.surface: An actor taking his bow at the end of a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes a bow' suggests a curtain call; here the bow is the archer's weapon. A pantomime is a British festive stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary archer outlaw carries a longbow and is a common pantomime title role.

clue.text: Biscuit that should be on the table tomorrow

definitions.meaning: a thin crisp savoury biscuit eaten with cheese

definitions.text: that should be on the table tomorrow
definitions.meaning: a paper tube that bangs when pulled, set at each place for the festive dinner

explanation.walkthrough: 'tomorrow' places the puzzle on Christmas Eve, when the festive table is laid with paper tubes that snap when pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crisp savoury biscuit and the paper tube pulled apart at the festive dinner table.

clue.text: Little certainty in company refusal to offer musical entertainment

indicators.note: in says the shortened word sits inside the word for refusal

parts.note: a refusal is a no
a cert is a shortened certainty, a sure thing

explanation.surface: A company doubtfully declining to put on a musical show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' shortens the word rather than meaning small: a cert is everyday British slang for a sure thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A work for soloist and orchestra is a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Caroller scored highly?

parts.note: a carol singer whose part is written in the highest range of the score

explanation.surface: A carol singer who did well in some contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored highly' sounds like winning marks; in music, a part is scored, here at the top of the vocal range.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest female or boy singing voice has its part written at the top of the musical score.

clue.text: Harks on about wrapping a vessel found in older book

indicators.note: wrapping says the shuffled letters enclose the letter a
about says the letters of harks on are shuffled around

parts.note: these two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: Someone harks on about wrapping a boat mentioned in an old book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges HARKS ON, and 'wrapping' puts the A inside it. 'older book' is the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The great boat built before the Flood appears in Genesis, the first book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Party performance of Parisian, with cleaner answer given first

indicators.note: given first says the cleaner and answer come before the French word

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner
de is French for of, as a Parisian would say it

explanation.surface: A party turn put on by a Frenchman, with a cleaner's reply coming first.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is an old British word for a cleaning lady; 'given first' fixes the order of the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: The guessing game of acting out words in mime is a classic performance at family parties.

clue.text: Agreed time to enjoy 21 and 15s?

definitions.meaning: agreed means in harmony, of one mind
one o'clock is a time to sit down to the festive bird and pull the paper novelties at lunch

explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the festive bird and 15 the paper tubes pulled at the table, enjoyed at lunch, say one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in harmony with someone means being reconciled and in accord, which is what agreed means here.

clue.text: Country fare for 22

definitions.meaning: the nation spanning Anatolia and Thrace
the roast bird traditionally eaten at the festive dinner

explanation.walkthrough: '22' refers to the answer at 22, the festive season; 'fare' is food, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation straddling Europe and Asia shares its name with the large roast bird of the festive dinner.

clue.text: Queen maybe following Noel's seasonal message

indicators.note: following puts the playing card after the word for Noel

parts.note: Noel is another word for the festive season of the Nativity
a queen is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A monarch, perhaps, coming after Noel with a festive broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests the monarch's festive broadcast; here it is a queen among playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The greeting sent by post at the end of the year is a seasonal message of goodwill.

clue.text: Hurried to get to church after time, in a sleepy state

indicators.note: after says the remaining pieces follow the abbreviation for time

parts.note: hurried means ran
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to church late and arrived drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dazed, half-conscious condition is a sleepy state, as if hypnotised.

clue.text: Bedding down in the stable

parts.note: dried stalks are spread on a stable floor as bedding, as in the manger at the Nativity

explanation.surface: Settling in for the night in a stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bedding down' sounds like going to sleep; it is the bedding material laid on the stable floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried cereal stalks are the usual bedding laid for animals in a stable.

clue.text: Wise men's origin that is recorded in gold book

indicators.note: recorded in says the abbreviation is written inside the other pieces

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
NT is the New Testament, a book
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Where the wise men came from, as written in a golden book.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is 'or' in heraldry, a crossword staple; 'recorded in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi came from the East, and the old poetic name for the East is this word.

clue.text: Researcher, not Roman Catholic, arranged to run through Nativity play perhaps

indicators.note: arranged says the remaining letters of researcher are put in a new order

parts.note: the word researcher supplies the letters
RC is the abbreviation for Roman Catholic, and 'not' takes these letters away

explanation.surface: A researcher who isn't Catholic organised a practice of the school nativity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not Roman Catholic' takes R and C out of RESEARCHER, and 'arranged' rearranges RESEAHER. 'Nativity play perhaps' is an example of what is run through.
explanation.definitionFit: To practise a play before performing it is to go over it from start to finish.

clue.text: Way three kings travelled with a bit of a laugh from Santa's place in Devon

parts.note: the Magi travelled from the East, so they headed west

parts.words: a bit of a laugh from Santa's
parts.note: Santa's laugh is ho ho ho, and a bit of it is one ho

explanation.surface: The route of the three kings, with a chuckle from Father Christmas, leads to a Devon spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Westward Ho! is a seaside village in Devon, a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Devon village is named after Charles Kingsley's novel, and is a real place in that county.

clue.text: See 22
